title: ALIGN: Word Association Learning for Cultural Alignment in Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the alignment of Large Language Models' responses with human population-level distributions on religious belief survey questions from the World Values Survey. This included questions about belief in God, Heaven, Hell, and the afterlife, comparing model answers to survey data from the US and China.
findings: Fine-tuning models on cultural word associations effectively shifted their responses on religious belief questions (e.g., belief in God, Heaven, afterlife) to better align with the target culture's (US vs. China) survey data. For instance, after fine-tuning on Chinese data, a model's prediction for belief in 'Heaven' shifted from 71% 'Yes' to 82% 'No', closely matching the Chinese human response of 88% 'No'. The fine-tuned models also captured more nuanced, culture-specific spiritual concepts, such as associating 'death' with 'reincarnation' (轮回), reflecting a deeper value alignment.
references: Anurag Acharya, Kartik Talamadupula, and Mark Finlayson. 2021. Toward an atlas of cultural common-sense for machine reasoning.
